Northumberland: England's Last Wilderness on Two Wheels

Northumberland is England's least populated county and it feels like it. Vast, empty moorlands stretch to the horizon, Hadrian's Wall marches across wild hilltops, and the coastline is a succession of sandy bays and castle-topped headlands. For motorcyclists seeking solitude and space, Northumberland is unmatched in England.

Hadrian's Wall Road

The B6318 Military Road follows the line of Hadrian's Wall from Chollerford to Greenhead. Built in the 18th century directly on top of the Roman wall (much to archaeologists' dismay), it's a rolling, undulating road across high moorland with stunning views in every direction. The wall and its forts appear regularly along the route — stop at Housesteads for the best-preserved section.

Northumberland Coast

The A1 and B1340 along the Northumberland coast pass through some of England's most beautiful coastal scenery. Bamburgh Castle, Holy Island (accessible by causeway at low tide), and the Farne Islands are all visible from the road. The beaches are vast, empty, and backed by dunes — this is English coastal riding at its finest.

Kielder and the North Tyne Valley

The road to Kielder Water through the North Tyne Valley is a proper adventure. Kielder is England's largest forest and most remote village — the roads are narrow, winding, and often deserted. The reservoir is enormous and surrounded by dark forest. The area holds England's darkest skies — return after dark and the stars are extraordinary.

Northumberland feels like Scotland without crossing the border. The emptiness is genuine — some roads see fewer than 50 vehicles a day.

Classic Northumberland Loop

Start from Hexham and ride the Military Road west to Greenhead. Head north through Bellingham to Kielder, then east across the Cheviot foothills to Wooler. South through Alnwick to the coast at Amble, then back via Rothbury and Hexham. This 150-mile loop covers the best of Northumberland in a full day.

More Routes Worth Riding

  • A68 Carter Bar — Crosses the border into Scotland at 418 metres with panoramic views
  • A696 to Jedburgh — Flowing road through rolling Cheviot foothills
  • Coquet Valley — Quiet lanes following the River Coquet through Rothbury to Alwinton
  • B6341 Alnwick to Rothbury — Beautiful moorland road via Thrunton Wood

Practical Information

Fuel is available in Hexham, Alnwick, Morpeth, and Wooler, but remote areas like Kielder have no fuel stations — plan accordingly. Road surfaces vary; main roads are good but minor roads can be rough. Northumberland is accessible from Newcastle (30 minutes to the park boundary) and makes an excellent weekend trip from northern England or southern Scotland. Some roads see fewer than 50 vehicles a day, so it delivers Scottish-style emptiness without crossing the border.
